recentMedia.caption:
By the end of junior year, 76% of Power 4 players are already committed.

That is most of the top level, gone before senior year even starts. Other D1 is slower. Only 44% commit that early. Most of the rest go during senior fall.

D2, D3, and NAIA move later still. Just 5% commit by the end of junior year. Then 66% commit during senior fall. That fall runs from August to December. October and November alone are more than half of those commits.

So the levels do not all move at once. The top goes early. The rest fills in later.

If your son is a junior aiming high, the clock is already running. If he is looking at D2, D3, or NAIA, this fall is his window. The middle player there commits in November of senior year.

Know where he stands now. The free Fit Check gives you a range and his top 3 schools he should reach out to, and why. 

Comment “FIT” and I’ll send it over to you, or get it at the link in our bio!

#baseballrecruiting #collegebaseball #travelball #baseballparents #highschoolbaseball

Every parent in this sport is trying to answer one question. Where does my kid actually fit?

You can’t get a straight answer, because almost everyone you ask has a reason to keep you hopeful. His coach wants him to stay. The showcase wants the entry fee. The service wants you to renew.

So we built the honest version and made it free. It’s called the Fit Check.

He puts in his numbers, his grades, and what he wants in a school. About five minutes later you get three things:

Where his numbers land right now, as a range next to the real players committing at his position.

Three schools that actually fit him, with the coach to write to and a first email drafted in his voice that he sends himself.

And where he sits on the commit clock, so you finally know if he’s early or behind.

No credit card, no sales call. It’s the same read paying families get, narrowed to his top three schools.

Comment FIT and I’ll send you the link, or grab it in our bio.

BaseballPath reads your metrics against the 50,000+ college players behind every eval and gives you an honest range, like mid D2 to high D3, plus the schools that actually fit you athletically and academically.

Sending your stats to 100 coaches isn't exposure. It's noise.

Coaches can tell when a kid copy-pasted the same email to every program, and they ignore it. Same with showing up to a random camp where the coach never asked for you. That's time and money you don't get back.

A player told me on a call last week: if the coach doesn't actually want you there, you're just wasting your time and money. He's right.

Fit beats volume. Figure out your real range first (low D1, high D2, wherever you actually land), then email the 10 schools that make sense instead of the 100 that don't. Players who target programs that recruit kids like them get real replies. Everyone else gets silence.
